text: The Procuring Entity requests proposals for the supply and technical validation of electrical equipment. Each bidder shall identify eligible products, state compliance with every mandatory requirement, provide objective evidence, and complete the product-response and evaluation columns in the companion Excel workbook.

The product master is a procurement baseline, not a bidder's self-declaration and not evidence of compliance. Where a comparison value is marked as assumed, it must be replaced with verified manufacturer data in the bidder response.
Completed Excel response matrix for every offered product and product-family requirement.
Manufacturer product datasheet and a complete bill of materials for every offered item.
Applicable IEC/ANSI/UL standards, declarations, certificates, and test reports.
Clause-by-clause compliance statement; “Comply”, “Exception”, or “Not applicable” is required.
Commercial proposal showing unit price, quantity, delivery term, warranty, and validity period.
Manufacturer authorization, production facility information, after-sales organization, and technical support plan.
Factory acceptance, type/routine test plan, packing, inspection, delivery, and commissioning approach.
Evidence for maintenance interval, service life, warranty, spare parts, and lifecycle support.
The bidder shall complete one response row per offered product. A numeric or text response without a cited source is not accepted as evidence.

Product-master records marked comparison_values_assumed=Y contain demonstration or synthesized comparison values. These values shall not be treated as guarantees, test results, catalog ratings, or contractual requirements. The bidder must verify, replace, or reject every applicable assumed value with manufacturer documentation.
The evaluated price shall include transportation, insurance, installation supervision and commissioning for each offered GIS bay.
The bidder shall submit a separately priced list of recommended spare parts for five (5) years of operation.
The evaluated price shall state the currency, price validity period and payment milestones for the complete scope of supply.
Type Test reports issued by an independent accredited laboratory shall be submitted for the offered GIS.
Routine Test shall be performed on every GIS bay at the factory and shall be witnessed by the Procuring Entity.
The bidder shall submit the factory test report and the inspection and test plan at least four (4) weeks before shipment.
The manufacturer shall hold a valid ISO 9001 certificate for the production facility of the offered equipment.
The bidder shall have at least ten (10) years of experience in manufacturing and supplying gas-insulated switchgear.
An authorization letter from the manufacturer shall be submitted with the proposal.
Any deviation that is not listed in the bidder's deviation schedule shall be deemed to be accepted by the bidder.
No deviations from the technical requirements will be accepted after contract award.
The scope of supply shall cover all accessories required for safe operation, including but not limited to special tools, earthing devices and gas handling equipment.
Any item that is not explicitly mentioned but is necessary for the complete installation shall be supplied at no extra cost to the Procuring Entity.
The annual gas leakage rate of each gas compartment of the GIS shall not exceed 0.5 %.
